Here’s a quick roundup of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thrillers that hit theaters or streaming services in 2020. All of them earned strong reviews, solid box‑office numbers (where applicable), and/or high audience approval ratings.

| # | Title | Release (theatrical/streaming) | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|---------------------------------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **Tenet** | May 31 2020 (limited theatrical & HBO Max) | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson, Elizabeth Debicki | A mind‑bending heist thriller that blends time‑travel mechanics with slick action choreography. Its complex narrative structure and high production values made it a standout even amid pandemic‑induced theater closures. |
| 2 | **The Invisible Man** | July 24 2020 (limited theatrical & Peacock) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern retelling of H.G. Wells’ classic, this film mixes psychological horror with crime‑thriller pacing. Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as a woman hunted by her abusive ex‑partner who uses technology to stay unseen. |
| 3 | **The Gentlemen** | August 28 2020 (limited theatrical & Amazon Prime Video) | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced dialogue and stylish visuals shine in this British gangster caper. The film balances humor with tense plot twists, earning praise for its sharp script and ensemble cast. |
| 4 | **Uncut Gems** | September 18 2020 (limited theatrical & Netflix) | Ben Safdie, Joshua Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett, Jennifer Lawrence | Though more of a crime drama, its relentless pacing and Sandler’s manic performance make it feel like a thriller. The film’s chaotic energy and moral ambiguity kept audiences on edge. |
| 5 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | October 23 2020 (limited theatrical & Netflix) | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller. Sorkin’s razor‑sharp dialogue and the film’s historical relevance gave it both critical acclaim and audience engagement. |
| 6 | **The Hunt** | November 20 2020 (limited theatrical & Hulu) | Craig Zobel | Mark Strong, Olivia Colman | A dark satire that turns into a tense thriller when a group of men hunt a young boy for sport. The film’s unsettling premise and strong performances earned it a cult following. |
| 7 | **The Irishman** | December 25 2020 (limited theatrical & Netflix) | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | While primarily a crime epic, its investigative narrative and use of de-aging tech create a suspenseful atmosphere. Scorsese’s masterful storytelling and the star‑studded cast made it a must‑watch. |

### Quick Tips for Watching

* **Streaming Platforms:** Most of these films were released on major streaming services (HBO Max, Peacock, Amazon Prime Video, Netflix, Hulu). Check your local availability; some may have moved to other platforms after their initial window.
* **Critical Scores:** Rotten Tomatoes “Tomatometer” scores range from 70%–95%, while IMDb ratings hover between 7.0–8.5/10. These metrics reflect broad consensus among critics and general viewers alike.
* **Genre Blends:** Many of the entries blend sub‑genres—psychological horror, satire, courtroom drama—so you’ll get a richer experience than a straight‑up crime thriller.

Enjoy diving into these gripping stories!
